claims.title: Exact fixed-model policy-vector frontier recursion
claims.scope: a finite family of complete rational hidden-Markov source models, one model selected once for the full horizon, public observations, deterministic zero-error prefix-code actions, finite horizon, and rational switching penalty
assumptions: the selected model identity remains fixed across every observation history
model transitions and observation kernels are code-independent
one public continuation policy is shared by all active models capable of emitting the same observation
all frontier combinations and dominance checks complete below declared caps
nonclaims: the theorem supplies no prior probability over model labels
the finite model family is not a confidence region unless separately calibrated
the result is not evidence for simulation or a parent-resource bound

claims.title: Rectangular model reselection upper-bounds fixed-model ambiguity
claims.scope: the fixed-model minimax game and the scalar rectangular relaxation built from the same model family, observations, code actions, horizon, and switching cost
assumptions: the rectangular recursion may maximize over the active model set again at every public node
the fixed-model recursion preserves one common model coordinate for the entire expected-cost calculation
nonclaims: the rectangular game is a stronger ambiguity hypothesis rather than a conservative implementation of the same fixed-model hypothesis

claims.title: Public observations update model-conditional beliefs and eliminate only zero-likelihood models
claims.scope: positive-probability observation branches in the declared finite rational model family
assumptions: each active model applies its own transition and observation probabilities
a model remains active after an observation exactly when that observation has positive probability under the model
nonclaims: model elimination is logical under the supplied exact probabilities and is not a finite-sample statistical rejection guarantee
no posterior probability over model labels is introduced

claims.title: Componentwise dominance pruning preserves the fixed-model frontier
claims.scope: expected continuation-cost vectors indexed by the still-active fixed models at one public state
assumptions: one vector is no larger in every active-model coordinate and strictly smaller in at least one
parent operations use nonnegative model-specific observation probabilities, nonnegative stage-cost addition, and a final maximum over model coordinates
nonclaims: Pareto pruning does not prevent exponential frontier growth
dominance would need to be reconsidered if omitted constraints or rewards were not represented in the cost vector

claims.title: No-signal K3 has fixed-model value five and rectangular value six
claims.scope: three one-state point-mass source models, complete confusion K3, one common uninformative observation, three periods, zero switching cost, and complete binary prefix codes
assumptions: nature selects one of the three models once in the fixed-model game
the rectangular relaxation may reselect the worst active model at later nodes
nonclaims: the one-unit gap is specific to the declared bounded instance
the example does not imply that any physical simulator changes models

claims.title: A noisy model-discriminating signal has strict intermediate robust value
claims.scope: two one-state point-mass K3 models, one-period horizon, zero switching cost, and no, symmetric noisy, and fully revealing public signals
assumptions: the noisy signal has conditional probabilities three quarters versus one quarter under the two models
one public code action is selected after observing the signal
nonclaims: the values two, five quarters, and one are specific to the declared model family
the observation kernel is supplied rather than estimated

claims.title: Bounded exact fixed-model frontier and rectangular-relaxation audit
claims.scope: the fixed-versus-rectangular K3, noisy-signal, zero-likelihood elimination, duplicate-model, validation, and frontier-cap cases exercised by repository tests
assumptions: all code candidates, public belief states, continuation combinations, frontier entries, and dominance comparisons complete below configured caps
all probabilities and costs use exact rational arithmetic
nonclaims: bounded finite completion is not a polynomial-time scalability theorem
CI success is not empirical evidence for simulation
